summary: CKGSB's global marketing is pivoting hard toward AI/chat-search visibility for Asia Star and the new Intelligent China program, while simultaneously pushing the Knowledge website redesign toward launch and standing up the Women in Leadership Forum.
summaryDetail: The single most important thread is the SEO/AI-visibility strategy: Asia Star and Intelligent China are the top two programs to promote (US partners Stanford/Columbia on hold, Berkeley a possible third), and Joseph owes the target areas/prompts for AI search plus the Google Analytics conversion-tracking documentation, with the team analyzing Asia Star participant profiles and CRM hot leads. In parallel, the Knowledge website redesign is nearing launch on the current layout with menu-categorization improvements and an editorial-style article display—Joseph to share the HTML and run a 30-minute feedback session, Joker to implement changes, and remaining fixes (publication news, She Innovates consistency, whiteboard-style frame lines) to close before go-live. This week's urgent items are the Intelligent China webpage launch and traffic push, plus the Women in Leadership Forum logistics—finalizing Ira's women's-figures data, parking/settlement arrangements, and the on-stage video decision. Also pending: the English obituary for Professor Jon Liao, and a housekeeping Outlook account lockout cleanup (re-add accounts, update passwords across devices, confirm backend unlock with CKGSB).
